accepted.s: Article 21A of the Constitution provides for free and compulsory education to children in which age group?
accepted.x: Article 21A guarantees free and compulsory education to all children from 6 to 14 years of age.
accepted.tq: Use the precise constitutional age range to distinguish Article 21A from Articles 45 and 51A(k).
accepted.sec: Right to Education - Article 21A, inserting amendment and commencement, RTE Act 2009, earlier cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Article 21A was inserted into the Constitution by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
accepted.x: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A.
accepted.tq: Split the amendment-number and year combination from nearby constitutional amendments.
accepted.sec: Right to Education - Article 21A, inserting amendment and commencement, RTE Act 2009, earlier cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, along with Article 21A, came into force on:
accepted.x: The RTE Act, 2009 and Article 21A came into force on 1 April 2010.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the enactment year and the commencement date.
accepted.sec: Right to Education - Article 21A, inserting amendment and commencement, RTE Act 2009, earlier cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Right to Education Act, 2009:
1. It provides for 25 per cent entry-level seats in unaided private schools for children belonging to weaker groups.
2. The 25 per cent provision applies to minority schools without exception.
3. The Act has been amended in 2012, 2017, 2019 and 2022.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Act provides 25 per cent entry-level seats in unaided private schools for weaker groups, but the provision does not apply to minority schools. It was amended in 2012, 2017, 2019 and 2022.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong statement by testing the absolute claim about minority schools.
accepted.sec: Right to Education - Article 21A, inserting amendment and commencement, RTE Act 2009, earlier cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Article 21A — Early childhood care below six years
Article 45 — Free and compulsory education from six to fourteen years
Article 51A(k) — Duty of parent or guardian to provide educational opportunities to a child or ward aged six to fourteen years
Article 21 — Reservation of entry-level seats in private schools
accepted.x: Article 51A(k) imposes the duty on a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to a child or ward between 6 and 14 years. Article 21A concerns that age group as a Fundamental Right, while Article 45 concerns early childhood care below six years.
accepted.tq: Match each constitutional provision with its correct subject and age group.
accepted.sec: Right to Education - Article 21A, inserting amendment and commencement, RTE Act 2009, earlier cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, consider the following statements:
1. It inserted Article 21A.
2. It modified Article 45 to concern early childhood care and education below six years.
3. It inserted Article 51A(k) relating to the educational opportunities of children aged 6 to 14 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 86th Amendment made all three changes: it inserted Article 21A, changed Article 45 and added the parental duty under Article 51A(k).
accepted.tq: Recognise the common amendment behind three related constitutional provisions.
accepted.sec: Right to Education - Article 21A, inserting amendment and commencement, RTE Act 2009, earlier cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right under Article 21A?
o: Free elementary education for children aged 6 to 14 years
Education in the manner determined by the State
Free higher education for all citizens
Compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years
accepted.x: Article 21A covers only free and compulsory elementary education for children aged 6 to 14 years. Higher and professional education are not Fundamental Rights under Article 21A.
accepted.tq: Identify the excluded level of education rather than being distracted by the constitutional wording.
accepted.sec: Right to Education - Article 21A, inserting amendment and commencement, RTE Act 2009, earlier cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The phrase “in such manner as the State may determine” in Article 21A indicates that:
o: The right applies only when the State has sufficient financial resources
The State may decide whether education is a Fundamental Right
The State may decide the manner of providing free and compulsory education
Only local bodies may provide elementary education
accepted.x: Article 21A makes education a Fundamental Right while leaving the manner of its provision to be determined by the State.
accepted.tq: Separate the existence of a Fundamental Right from the manner in which it is implemented.
accepted.sec: Right to Education - Article 21A, inserting amendment and commencement, RTE Act 2009, earlier cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Section 3 of the Right to Education Act, 2009, principally provides that:
o: The State may replace elementary education with vocational training for all children
Every child aged 6 to 14 years has a right to free and compulsory education in a neighbourhood school until completion of elementary education
Only children admitted to minority schools are entitled to free education
Every adult has a right to free professional education in any State institution
accepted.x: Section 3 gives every child aged 6 to 14 years the right to free and compulsory education in a neighbourhood school until elementary education is completed.
accepted.tq: Recall the operative provision by identifying its beneficiary, age group, institution and educational level.
accepted.sec: Right to Education - Article 21A, inserting amendment and commencement, RTE Act 2009, earlier cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Right to Education Act, 2009, schools are reimbursed on the basis of:
o: The total number of teachers appointed
The number of children completing secondary education
The annual income of the school management
accepted.x: Schools covered by the RTE framework are reimbursed on the basis of per-child expenditure.
accepted.tq: Test the exact basis of reimbursement rather than the broader objective of the Act.
accepted.sec: Right to Education - Article 21A, inserting amendment and commencement, RTE Act 2009, earlier cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which institutions are associated with review and redress of grievances under the Right to Education framework?
o: Election Commission and State Election Commissions
UPSC and State Public Service Commissions
Finance Commission and State Finance Commissions
accepted.x: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights and State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights review and address grievances under the framework. Their statutory basis is associated with the CPCR Act, 2005.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-function association to eliminate bodies with unrelated constitutional roles.
accepted.sec: Right to Education - Article 21A, inserting amendment and commencement, RTE Act 2009, earlier cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to the right to education in chronological order:
A. Unnikrishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh
B. Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka
C. 86th Constitutional Amendment Act
D. Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act
accepted.x: Mohini Jain was decided in 1992, Unnikrishnan in 1993, the 86th Amendment was enacted in 2002, and the RTE Act was enacted in 2009.
accepted.tq: Fix the sequence using the dated judicial decisions followed by the amendment and enabling legislation.
accepted.sec: Right to Education - Article 21A, inserting amendment and commencement, RTE Act 2009, earlier cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding important cases on the right to education:
1. Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka was decided in 1992.
2. Mohini Jain held that the right to education flows from Article 21.
3. Unnikrishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh held that free education is available only up to 14 years, with education beyond that depending on the State’s economic capacity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the years and rulings in Mohini Jain and Unnikrishnan. These decisions preceded the constitutional insertion of Article 21A.
accepted.tq: Combine the year, case name and holding, checking each statement independently.
accepted.sec: Right to Education - Article 21A, inserting amendment and commencement, RTE Act 2009, earlier cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The constitutional status of the Right to Education is best described as follows:
o: It is a Fundamental Duty of parents alone
It is only a Directive Principle of State Policy
It is a statutory right unrelated to Article 21
It is a Fundamental Right and is treated as an extension of the right to life
accepted.x: The Right to Education is a Fundamental Right under Article 21A and is treated as an extension of the right to life under Article 21.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Fundamental Right from the related Directive Principle and parental Fundamental Duty.
accepted.sec: Right to Education - Article 21A, inserting amendment and commencement, RTE Act 2009, earlier cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The right to privacy was declared to be intrinsic to life and personal liberty under Article 21 in:
o: Gobind v. State of Madhya Pradesh
Kharak Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
accepted.x: In K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, decided in 2017, the Supreme Court held that privacy is intrinsic to life and personal liberty under Article 21 and protected under Part III.
accepted.tq: Identify the authoritative later case rather than the earlier cases that only raised or partially recognised privacy concerns.
accepted.sec: Right to privacy - article, Puttaswamy bench, cases overruled, tests  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The judgment in K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India was delivered on:
accepted.x: The Puttaswamy privacy judgment was delivered on 24 August 2017.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact judgment date from nearby constitutional and subsequent privacy-law dates.
accepted.sec: Right to privacy - article, Puttaswamy bench, cases overruled, tests  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the bench and conclusion in K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India?
o: A nine-judge bench unanimously recognised privacy as intrinsic to life and personal liberty
A seven-judge bench unanimously held that privacy is outside Part III
A five-judge bench by a majority held that privacy is only a statutory right
A nine-judge bench held that privacy is available only to citizens
accepted.x: A unanimous nine-judge bench recognised privacy as intrinsic to life and personal liberty and protected under Article 21 and Part III.
accepted.tq: Check the bench strength, unanimity and constitutional status together.
accepted.sec: Right to privacy - article, Puttaswamy bench, cases overruled, tests  [APPSC]

accepted.s: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India overruled M.P. Sharma and Kharak Singh to the extent that those decisions:
o: Recognised proportionality as the sole test for all restrictions
Denied the existence of privacy as a protected constitutional interest
Declared education to be a Directive Principle
accepted.x: Puttaswamy overruled M.P. Sharma (1954) and Kharak Singh (1962) insofar as they denied privacy as a constitutional protection.
accepted.tq: Focus on the limited extent of overruling instead of treating the earlier judgments as wholly erased.
accepted.sec: Right to privacy - article, Puttaswamy bench, cases overruled, tests  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to the evolution of the right to privacy?
o: M.P. Sharma — 2017 recognition of privacy as intrinsic to Article 21
Kharak Singh — early concern relating to privacy
Gobind — denial that privacy forms part of liberty
Puttaswamy — privacy limited to a statutory entitlement
accepted.x: Kharak Singh represents an early concern relating to privacy. Gobind v. State of Madhya Pradesh in 1975 recognised privacy as part of liberty, while Puttaswamy gave privacy comprehensive constitutional protection.
accepted.tq: Use the chronological development of the doctrine to separate early concern, partial recognition and final constitutional affirmation.
accepted.sec: Right to privacy - article, Puttaswamy bench, cases overruled, tests  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
For an intrusion into the right to privacy to withstand constitutional scrutiny, which of the following requirements are relevant?
1. Legality, meaning the existence of a law.
2. A legitimate aim or need.
3. Proportionality.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The privacy restriction framework includes legality, legitimate aim or need and proportionality. All three requirements are relevant to assessing an intrusion.
accepted.tq: Recognise the cumulative constitutional test instead of selecting only the most familiar element.
accepted.sec: Right to privacy - article, Puttaswamy bench, cases overruled, tests  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A government measure restricts personal data without any supporting law, although it claims to pursue a public objective. Which requirement of the privacy test is most clearly absent?
accepted.x: The legality requirement demands that an intrusion into privacy be supported by a law. A claimed public objective cannot substitute for the existence of legal authority.
accepted.tq: Apply the first step of the privacy test by asking whether the restriction has a legal basis.
accepted.sec: Right to privacy - article, Puttaswamy bench, cases overruled, tests  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 is associated with which institution?
accepted.x: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 provides for a Data Protection Board. The enacted law is an Act, not merely a Personal Data Protection Bill.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the enacted statute and the earlier bill terminology, and identify its associated body.
accepted.sec: Right to privacy - article, Puttaswamy bench, cases overruled, tests  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The proportionality requirement in privacy jurisprudence was subsequently applied in the context of Aadhaar in:
accepted.x: The proportionality framework developed in privacy jurisprudence was subsequently applied to Aadhaar in 2018.
accepted.tq: Separate the year of the Puttaswamy judgment from the year of its later application to Aadhaar.
accepted.sec: Right to privacy - article, Puttaswamy bench, cases overruled, tests  [APPSC]
